name: K16 turbine wheel, IN718 F0 concept
description: Clean-sheet concept of a twelve-blade K16 hot rotor to screen the value and limits of an IN718 LPBF route. The diameters, blade count and part reference come from supplier catalogues; all profiles and interfaces remain hypothetical.

classification.intended_use: F0 screening of CAD, rotation, overspeed, thermal, turbine power, expansion, imbalance and cycles; no manufacturing, rotation, installation or engine start authorized

provenance.record_license: MIT for the concept, the script and the calculations; no photograph, Porsche illustration, BorgWarner/Kinugawa surface or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - 993 turbocharger context
sources.notes: Confirms interest in 993 hot-side upgrades and states that no additive housing or rotor is catalogued. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-K16-COMPRESSOR-WHEEL-CANDIDATE.

sources.title: TurboMaster - K16 5316-988-6735
sources.notes: Links the right K16 to turbine wheel 5316-120-5000. See SRC-TURBOMASTER-993-K16-6735-PARTS.

sources.title: Invasion Auto Products - stated internal data of the right K16
sources.notes: States 54.96/48.97 mm and twelve blades for 5316-120-5000. See SRC-INVASIONAUTOPRODUCTS-993-K16-INTERNAL-DATA.

sources.title: Kinugawa - replacement K16 wheel
sources.notes: States 49/55 mm, twelve blades, 9.4 mm height and 8.42 mm shaft for the same reference; no surface or tolerance. See SRC-KINUGAWA-K16-TURBINE-WHEEL-53161205000.

sources.title: EOS NickelAlloy IN718 API for EOS M 290, 40 micrometers
sources.notes: Process data and room-temperature coupons for the candidate material; no rotor qualification. See SRC-EOS-IN718-API-M290-40UM.

sources.title: BorgWarner - Performance Turbocharger Catalog
sources.notes: 993 Turbo context and T3 of 950 °C continuous / 980 °C transient for the upgrade line; this is not the metal temperature of the K16 wheel. See SRC-BORGWARNER-993-K16-PERFORMANCE-CATALOG.

material.grade: EOS NickelAlloy IN718 API, M290 40 µm, heat treated for comparison
material.standard: UNS N07718; program-specific rotor, process, heat treatment and allowables specification to be contracted

post_processing: blade orientation and supports to be qualified against the recoater
traced stress relief, solution treatment, gas quench and aging
HIP to be decided on defects, creep, toughness, HCF and burst
machining of the shaft interface, back face, datums and allowances
controlled profiling and polishing of blades and fillets
wheel-to-shaft joining process or one-piece shaft to be qualified
individual then rotor balancing, spin proof and contained overspeed
supplier_requirements: traceable EOS M290 machine, IN718 API parameter set, software, parameters, powder and lot
oriented coupons with tensile, HCF, LCF, creep, rupture, toughness and crack growth at temperature
distortion witnesses and capability after finishing of the 0.8 mm tips
full CT before and after machining with zoned defect criteria
FPI, metallography, microstructure, hardness, roughness and residual stresses
metrology of profiles, fillets, interface, runout and polar inertia
high-speed balancing, overspeed, burst and containment before turbo bench testing

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Qualify the IN718 joint with the shaft, bearings, shields and housing, as well as diffusion, fretting, oxidation and differential expansion.

known_limits: Only reference 5316-120-5000, the diameters, twelve blades, tip height and shaft diameter are published, by replacement-part catalogues.
The 20 mm axial envelope, the disk, the hub and the straight four-step blades are synthetic.
The STEP excludes the full shaft, the weld, the aerodynamic profiles, fillets, clearances and balancing details.
The speed of 103,464 rpm comes from the synthetic F1 compressor point, not from a K16 measurement.
The F0 fails the root and thermal-gradient screens at the 1.5 threshold; the gas context also exceeds the generic range stated by EOS.
The EOS properties are room-temperature coupons of the API process, not hot HCF, creep or burst allowables.
The single-point power balance replaces neither a turbine map, nor rotating CFD, nor CHT, nor rotordynamics.
The STEP proves only a readable BREP and is authorized neither for manufacturing, nor rotation, nor turbo or engine use.
